collectionIntent: Authentic GIS screens and GIS-produced maps, especially New Zealand software and government applications; no precomputer historical maps

items.title: ArcMap displaying Manaaki Whenua WMS land-cover layers
items.credit: Manaaki Whenua Landcare Research; basemap includes LINZ source data.
items.licence: Manaaki Whenua source attribution and WMS data terms; basemap includes LINZ Crown copyright
items.dateDisplay: ArcGIS 10.0 tutorial; exact capture date unstated
items.sourceEvidence: Publisher's ArcGIS WMS tutorial explicitly identifies this as an ArcGIS layout view with WMS legend.
items.altText: ArcMap desktop GIS with a layer list on the left, a coloured New Zealand land-cover map in layout view and a legend.
items.caption: Manaaki Whenua WMS land-cover and topographic layers viewed in ArcMap. A later desktop example of standardised spatial data services, not a 1990s GIS installation.
items.context: An authentic ArcMap GIS interface using a live New Zealand WMS data service. Chapter 21 discusses distributed datasets, coordination and standards; the screenshot is a later implementation example.

items.title: QGIS displaying Manaaki Whenua WMS layers and legends
items.credit: Manaaki Whenua Landcare Research; basemap layers include LINZ copyright where shown.
items.licence: Manaaki Whenua source attribution and WMS data terms
items.dateDisplay: QGIS 3.4.3 tutorial; approximately 2019, exact capture date unstated
items.sourceEvidence: Publisher's QGIS 3.4.3 WMS tutorial labels this screenshot QGIS WMS Legend.
items.altText: QGIS application window showing the legend of a Manaaki Whenua web map service.
items.caption: QGIS 3.4.3 consuming Manaaki Whenua's WMS layers. The interface demonstrates open-source desktop GIS drawing on national science services.
items.context: Publisher-documented QGIS desktop interface, illustrating a 2019-era workflow rather than the earlier initial spread of open-source GIS.

items.title: Canterbury Maps datasets inside ArcGIS Desktop
items.licence: Publisher rights; source attributed (permission asserted by site owner)
items.dateDisplay: Pre-2025 case study; exact screen capture year unstated
items.sourceEvidence: Original case study calls figure 2 an ArcGIS Desktop screen showing Canterbury Maps data and basemap services.
items.altText: ArcGIS Desktop showing Canterbury Maps geospatial layers, with a long table of contents and a mapped coastal suburb in Christchurch.
items.caption: Aurecon engineering users working with Canterbury Maps datasets in ArcGIS Desktop, including mapped infrastructure and consent layers. This is a later application of council spatial services.
items.context: Directly labelled ArcGIS Desktop figure 2 in a Canterbury Maps case study, illustrating council GIS services in engineering rather than the 1989 initial council implementations.

items.title: Canterbury Maps web GIS viewer in an Aurecon case study
items.licence: Publisher rights; source attributed (permission asserted by site owner)
items.dateDisplay: Pre-2025 case study; exact screen capture year unstated
items.sourceEvidence: Original case study labels figure 1 as a web GIS viewer with data and imagery from Canterbury Maps.
items.altText: A web-based Canterbury GIS viewer displaying geospatial data and imagery.
items.caption: A Canterbury Maps browser GIS viewer, showing local authority spatial datasets accessible without specialist desktop software.
items.context: A publisher-described operational New Zealand web GIS example, related to the longer trend towards browser access to spatial information.

items.title: LINZ Data Service topographic layers in 2016
items.sourceName: National Library of New Zealand / LINZ
items.credit: LINZ Data Service screenshot, published in Aaron Jordan's 'The future of maps', National Library, 21 July 2016.
items.licence: Publisher rights; source attributed (permission asserted by site owner)
items.sourceEvidence: National Library article from 21 July 2016 illustrates LINZ Data Service layers and download tools.
items.altText: LINZ Data Service portal from 2016 showing searchable Topo50 map datasets, map layer listings and a New Zealand preview map.
items.caption: The LINZ Data Service as illustrated in July 2016, allowing users to find national spatial datasets and explore their geographic coverage.
items.context: Dated official 2016 illustration of GIS data discovery and public reuse, a later access platform following the earlier Topo50 release discussed nearby.

items.title: Digital topographic map production on a GIS screen, 2016
items.credit: Land Information New Zealand, image republished by RNZ in Alison Ballance's 21 April 2016 programme.
items.licence: LINZ/RNZ publication credit; source attributed (permission asserted by site owner)
items.sourceEvidence: RNZ feature interviews LINZ cartographers and shows digital map editing compared with paper-era cartography.
items.altText: Computer screen displaying a detailed LINZ digital topographic map of the Leigh and Torkington Bay area, with software panels around the map.
items.caption: A modern LINZ digital cartography screen used to maintain New Zealand topographic mapping, published by RNZ in April 2016.
items.context: Publisher-dated documentary image from RNZ's 2016 account of contemporary LINZ digital cartography. It does not depict the initial 1970s database conversion.

items.title: ArcView GIS 3.2 survey mapping and data table, 2002
items.credit: 2002 Esri User Conference paper 'Simple GIS Tools for Traffic and Transit Noise Studies', original figure.
items.licence: Publisher rights; source attributed (permission asserted by site owner)
items.sourceEvidence: Source is an original 2002 GIS user conference paper featuring ArcView GIS 3.2 survey point and attribute interfaces.
items.altText: ArcView GIS 3.2 interface displaying a highway survey map and an attribute table of survey points and coordinates.
items.caption: A genuine 2002 ArcView GIS 3.2 screen showing a spatial survey and coordinate table. This is an overseas software example, not a New Zealand GIS deployment.
items.context: Contemporary 2002 documentation of the ArcView desktop environment described in Chapter 22; the example data concern an overseas highway and are included only to illustrate software appearance.
